North Carolina has proposed a toll of $10 each way for a standard car on the free Hatteras–Ocracoke ferry, and a state law passed in July says tolls start January 1, 2027. By law, toll revenue goes to replacing vessels: the state says its ferry fleet is 22 boats with an average age of about 28 years. On the other side, residents have boarded first for about forty years, county officials say, and in the state's comment period "keeping priority boarding" was mentioned 290 times and "not tolling residents" 260 times (mentions, not people). Should the people who live on Ocracoke pay the toll too, or ride free? Say which side you lean toward, and say why. And tell us where you're watching from, and the longest line you've ever waited in. 👇
